messages:
edr-bot: EDR Alert (A-2026-4821) - Suspicious child process chain detected on maya-laptop. Process tree: pwsh(4821) -> rundll32(4932) -> msdt(4940). Tried reading /Users/maya/.config/aws/credentials and executed `aws kms decrypt`. File quarantined: /tmp/az123.exe. Priority: high.

maya: I'm in standup, that's my laptop. I didn't run anything unusual. I'll step away from the meeting and join this thread.

sam: @maya please DO NOT VPN into corp while we investigate. @lee can you isolate the host from the network? :warning:

lee: isolating host via MDM now (profile applied). Confirmed quarantine of /tmp/az123.exe and user session locked. Kickstarting full EDR scan + memory capture (collecting /proc snapshot and network pcap). ETA ~10m.

raj: heads-up, the suspicious binary appears to have invoked the AWS CLI to call KMS decrypt. I'm pulling CloudTrail for Decrypt events for alias/redwood-prod-kms and the maya principal.

maya: I did use the AWS CLI yesterday morning for a dev test but not today. I did install a gem earlier this week though.

sam: @maya if you can, do NOT interact with the host. @lee can we capture the quarantine report MD5 so we can hit search across other endpoints?

lee: quarantine report shows md5: 9b2c7f4d8a1e6c3b5f2a9d0e6c7b8a12. Adding to telemetry and YARA hunt.

maya: copying md5 from the EDR alert: `9b2c7f4d8a1e6c3b5f2a9d0e6c7b8a12`

lee: lookup indicates match to 'tiny-updater' coinminer family in our threat intel feed. Treating as confirmed compromise for host. Initiating reprovision workflow and issuing loaner.

edr-bot: EDR note: file quarantined, credential caches cleared, user session locked. No successful outbound connections observed during the capture window (pcap shows attempted DNS to suspicious domains but no SYN to exfil hosts).

raj: CloudTrail: no KMS Decrypt events from maya@redwood in the last 24h. That suggests the local process used cached creds or local key material rather than making a successful Decrypt call to our KMS. I'm going to request an immediate rotation for the impacted key and revoke any long-lived secrets issued to maya.

sam: create an incident ticket (include artifacts: quarantine file, memory dump, timeline). Escalate to P2; if we find exfil evidence we escalate to P1 and notify execs. @maya, when you're off the laptop, rotate SSO + any API keys you have and confirm once complete.

maya: understoood. I'll hand the device to @it for pickup. Anything else I should do for my personal accounts?

lee: standard: reimage/wipe and preserve forensic artifacts. We'll take a memory dump and store it in the incident bucket. Personal accounts: rotate passwords, revoke OAuth tokens, check 2FA devices. We'll provide an FAQ.

sam: post-incident checklist being tracked in INS-2026-1123: 1) isolate host (done), 2) collect artifacts (edr quarantine + memory dump) (in progress), 3) hunt across fleet for MD5 and indicators (in progress), 4) rotate affected KMS keys and disable suspect IAM tokens (raj), 5) user remediation and reimage (lee), 6) postmortem and IOCs publish.

raj: ticket INS-2026-1123 created and populated with CloudTrail + KMS audit screenshots and the quarantine artifact. Proposing immediate rotation for alias/redwood-prod-kms; will coordinate maintenance window with infra.

maya: thanks everyone for the fast response. Please let me know when loaner is ready.

lee: loaner reserved. Tentative pickup window 1719127200 (UTC). We'll reassign user after reimage and close the incident thread once artifacts uploaded and rotation scheduled.

sam: closing loop here in this thread; will update INS-2026-1123 with final notes after key rotation and fleet hunt results. :thumbsup:
